summary: The batch is clean on length and gore, and the move names mostly respect the mechanics, but it is the more formulaic of the two. 87 Legendaries use the banned 'for N years / still has its original / never once' formula, and about 40 Rares and Epics are competence as a power (found the fuse, timed every race, guided the fleet, scanned the albums, sharpened every knife, recorded every episode) rather than trouble. The near-identical clusters collide hard: storage (hard disc L, hard drive R and external drive R all 'saved the file nobody backed up'; external, flash drive and memory card all 'survived a disaster, every file still there'; hard disc U and memory card U 'says it is full just when...'; flash drive R and USB key R 'internet went down'; USB key, USB stick and printer Legendaries all 'every school project for years'); timers ('timed every X without a mistake' Epics); compasses ('guided everyone through fog with no wrong turn', 'still points north'); remotes and fobs (pocket presses, 'everything on the street at once', whole-family sofa searches); razors ('every bathroom on the street at once' on electric razor, razor and toothbrush); comb and hair brush (identical 'tugs every tangle, ow'); drone and drone controller (same park light show); docking station and USB hub (same Legendary). Names are swapped on extractor fan, electric toothbrush and pill box, and do not describe their lore on GPS R, hinge R, carpet cleaner R, e-ink R, lighter E and razor C ('Neckniker'). Safety: the lighter and zippo Rare/Epic/Legendary centre on lighting flames and copy w08 matches; the Nerf Uncommon fires at the cat; 'sniper', 'war', 'showdown', 'quick draw' and 'pump action' appear on toy guns; the pill box Legendary name echoes a song about pills. Brands and memes: Remingworth, Hoover, 'Windproof' (Zippo), 'goes up to eleven', and 'Red Light Flash' (an approved Pilot 01 move) reused. Mechanics slips: heat words on non-burn moves (Heat Wave Blast, Hot Valve Whiff, Hot Glue Slam), 'Daze' or 'Flash' on Ultimates whose variants do not stun (keyring, padlock key, stamp, car fob, pill box), and defence words on attack boosts. Near-copies of w07 (ski mask, slipper, lanyard) and w10 (mixing desk). Every high and medium issue has a concrete replacement; names are checked as unique against all curated files and the Pilot 01 proposal.

patterns.pattern: Legendary formula: 'Has done X for N years / for three generations / still has its original or first X / never once'. The lessons ban this; it is the default Legendary shape in this batch.
patterns.suggestion: Replace each with one concrete outrageous achievement plus a punchline (per-id issues). At most a handful of Legendaries per batch should open with 'Has'.

patterns.pattern: Epic crowd formulas: 'every X in the office/school/street at once', 'was passed round every...', 'with a hundred others'.
patterns.suggestion: Give each Epic one specific disruption with a consequence.

patterns.pattern: Competence-as-power: Rares and Epics where the gadget simply works brilliantly (found the fuse, timed every race, guided the fleet, scanned the album, sharpened every knife, recorded every episode). Rare should be a troublesome power, Epic large-scale chaos.
patterns.suggestion: Turn each success into trouble: the plotter draws everything bigger, the egg timer runs backwards, the RAM stick tattles.

patterns.pattern: Monster names sit on the wrong rarity or do not describe their lore.
patterns.suggestion: Re-pair per the per-rarity name issues.

patterns.pattern: Storage cluster shares premises: 'saved the file its owner forgot to back up' (hard disc L, hard drive R, external drive R); 'survived a disaster, every file still there' (external L, flash drive C+L, memory card L); 'says it is full just when...' (hard disc U, memory card U); 'internet went down, carried the files' (flash drive R, USB key R); tiny and lost through the floorboards (memory card C, padlock key C); 'carried every school project for years' (USB key L, USB stick L, printer L).
patterns.suggestion: Keep hard disc L and external drive L; change the sibling sides as listed per id. Give each its own trait: SD card = trail camera only once, SIM = phone numbers, USB key = wrong way round, flash drive = laundry.

patterns.pattern: Timers and stopwatches all have 'timed/counted down every X without a mistake' Epics and 'timed every X for N years' Legendaries.
patterns.suggestion: Per-id replacements give each timer its own failure: sand running backwards, sunken cakes, false starts, a sports day until midnight.

patterns.pattern: Compasses (and the GPS) all have 'guided everyone through fog/ocean without a wrong turn' Epics and 'still points north/true' Legendaries.
patterns.suggestion: Compass = lost things and North Pole; small compass = snacks and a goose; ship compass = spoons and the map edge.

patterns.pattern: Remotes and fobs: accidental pocket presses, 'everything on the street at once when the signal went funny', and whole-family sofa searches repeat across garage remote, car fob, TV remote, cordless phone and contact lens case.
patterns.suggestion: Keep the garage remote's pocket press and the cordless phone's search; change the siblings.

patterns.pattern: Razors and shavers: 'every bathroom on the street at the same time' Epic appears on electric razor, razor and electric toothbrush; stubble on the sink appears on electric razor U and razor R. Blade words in razor moves.
patterns.suggestion: Change per id; keep blades out of move names.

patterns.pattern: Fire: x_lighter and x_zippo Rare/Epic/Legendary celebrate lighting candles, lanterns and campfires, and nearly copy w08 x_matches. Child safety.
patterns.suggestion: Use lid clacks, hiding from children, never being needed. No move or name about lighting.

patterns.pattern: Toy weapons: shooting at the cat, 'sniper', 'war', 'showdown', 'quick draw', 'pump action'. Child safety tone.
patterns.suggestion: No targeting pets or people's faces; use flags, foam, soaking and silliness instead of combat vocabulary.

patterns.pattern: Brands, memes and borrowed lines: Remingworth (Remington), 'Hoover', 'Windproof' (Zippo), 'goes up to eleven', 'Red Light Flash' (an approved Pilot 01 move), 'Little Helper' (song echo), 'press six times' (approved microwave joke). Object ids Chromebook, Zippo and Nerf are brands: keep them out of all display text.

Heat and status words that do not match mechanics: heat words on non-burn moves (Heat Wave Blast, Hot Valve Whiff, Hot Glue Slam), 'Daze/Flash' Ultimates whose variants do not stun, defence words on attack boosts (Bearing Lock, Hard Shell Boost, Wind Guard).
patterns.suggestion: Per-id replacements; varied Ultimates use effect-neutral names.

patterns.pattern: Near-copies of earlier drafts (w07, and the new w10).

Names disambiguated by bolting on the object word ('Batterybeep Aid', 'Dialspinner Phone', 'Upsidedowner Timer', 'Capdropper Key', 'Lidsnapper Lighter', 'Doorbeeper Fob', 'Pocketlost Fob', 'Strapsnapper Goggles', 'Blinkylights Box'), so near-duplicate names exist across objects.
patterns.suggestion: Coin a fresh name instead of suffixing.

patterns.pattern: Legendary name shape monoculture: 'Old Xworth/Xwell of the Y', 'Lady/Sir/Captain/Grand X of the Y' on most Legendaries.
patterns.suggestion: Vary shapes; the per-id replacements already break some up.
